paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm is teaching me: the LORD is holy, and that changes how we come to Him. He reigns, and the psalm says, "let the nations tremble!" (Psalm 99:1). It also says, "The mighty King loves justice" (Psalm 99:4). So He's not a ruler to shrug at, and He's not a ruler to run from either.

Now look at the people the psalm lifts up. Moses, Aaron and Samuel called, and the psalm says, "They called to the LORD and He answered" (Psalm 99:6), and they kept His decrees too (Psalm 99:7). Then the psalm tells God, "You were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their misdeeds" (Psalm 99:8). He forgives, and He still takes sin seriously, so both are true at the same time, and honestly, I'd be a mess with only one.

So the psalm ends with a call: "Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy" (Psalm 99:9). Baker, that's the big idea. Holiness is the reason we worship, and it's why we can come close, because this holy God answers when His people call. Hold Him high today, listen to what He says, and keep your oven ready for Him.
